result.title: How Language Models Organize Task Information
result.summary: Dense linear probes assess task readability from language model (LM) representations, but do not directly reveal how many features suffice for prediction. We measure readout sparsity with \(k^*\), the smallest feature count found by a fixed search protocol that recovers 95% of dense-probe AUROC above chance. We evaluate 19 LMs from five labs on 14 core tasks. Ten base models give the nine reliably readable tasks similar feature counts and nearly the same order. This agreement extends to the selected features themselves, which on three tasks show cross-model response correspondence beyond class-mean differences and a label-correlation-matched null. Instruction-tuned deployment selectively reduces \(k^*\), with both weights and input format contributing. In controlled synthetic experiments across 20 models, successfully learned targets admit single-feature readouts, whereas readable controls require tens of features. Reference-model \(k^*\) is associated with label requirements across eight students, following an empirical scaling of \(N^*\propto(k^*)^{0.65}\). After continual learning, saved heads can fail while linear readability remains high, and recovery requires fewer labels than initial task learning under the tested procedures. Pruning reduces linear readability, with wider pre-pruning readouts generally associated with larger losses. These findings distinguish task readability from readout sparsity and establish their complementary value for predicting learning requirements and diagnosing LM changes.

AI.brief_summary: 提出以 k*（固定搜索协议下恢复 95% dense-probe AUROC 所需的最少特征数）度量读出稀疏性，在 19 个语言模型、14 项任务上比较特征数与所选特征，并考察指令微调、合成任务、标签需求缩放及持续学习与剪枝后的变化。
AI.relevance_reason: 稀疏探针可读性度量或可借用于检验 VLM 内部状态是否保留视觉与任务必要信息，k* 与标签需求的经验缩放也可能为 latent 监督量估计提供线索，但该文仅涉及纯文本模型，迁移性需核查。
